A5 (EUF-CMA + 3 hardness shape axioms) remain cited-TCB per Barbosa et al. 2024. The Lean kernel built-ins (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound) are kernel-TCB. All three security claims are mathematically proven at the Lean kernel level, modulo the cited TCB axioms; theft_free's axiom closure is exactly {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, evm_bytecode_executes_correctly, precompile_0x02_is_FIPS_180_4, solidityVerifier_compiles_correctly, EUF_CMA_SPHINCSplusC, ITSR_F, SM_DT_TCR_F, hMsg_random_oracle, entrypoint_honest} (11), zero `sorry`, zero `True := trivial` theorem placeholders. (d) The Lean `validateSignature` model + `Factory.createAccountPrecondition` were made faithful to the deployed bytecode's ABI tail-pad check, audit-H-3 ownerIndex parity, and the install-time N-mask + duplicate-owner gates (previously the model accepted inputs the bytecode rejects). A3.2's axiom statement was tightened to carry the reachable-state hypothesis (the bytecode reverts on checked-arith overflow where the ℕ model returns failure — a divergence on UNREACHABLE states only). The bytecode-transported Lean corollaries `theft_free_bytecode` (closure += solidityWallet_compiles_correctly) and `factory_squat_defence_bytecode` (closure = solidityFactory_compiles_correctly + kernel) make the wallet/factory bridge axioms explicit in a `#print axioms`. The codehash pins are profile-aware (default runs=200 AND deploy runs=999999), both certified, plus an immutable-window lemma (`PinnedBytecodeImmutableLemma`) transporting the per-instance pin to all instances of a given profile modulo the two certified immutables. UPDATE 2026-06-10 (strengthened, this commit): (f) the full symbolic suite is now RUN against BOTH profiles' bytecode (run_halmos.sh runs default then deploy) — the prior 'control flow identical across profiles, single run covers both' shortcut is removed; the production runs=999999 bytecode is symbolically discharged directly. axioms.status_detail: Opaque-equality shape (load-bearing). HONEST LEDGER (UPDATED 2026-06-13 — A3.1 functional layer DISCHARGED; supersedes the 2026-06-11 false-as-stated correction). (1) DIGEST + htIdx sub-layers: EXECUTABLE Lean<->FIPS<->bytecode differential, 10/10 (HARD CHECK). (2) INPUT gates: Halmos length-revert + N-mask-reject on the deployed bytecode (codehash 0xf1ef…fef5), 3 rules. (3) FUNCTIONAL layer (FORS/WOTS+C/Merkle/hypertree over a 4008-byte sig): NOW an EXECUTABLE Lean<->bytecode KAT differential — `lake exe verify-test-vectors` runs `Spec.Signature.verify` over the byte-decoded signature and reports full-verify 10/10 (4 valid ACCEPTED, 6 negatives REJECTED), matching the deployed bytecode, as a HARD CHECK (requireFullVerify=true, non-zero exit on drift). The prior reconstruction-layer divergence was two real Lean-spec bugs, fixed 2026-06-13: (a) `chainHash` wrote the ADRS chain_index field instead of chain_pos (and clobbered the caller-set chain_index); (b) `loadWord32` returned an all-zero word when a 32-byte read window overran the 4008-byte blob, silently zeroing the last 16-byte auth-path entry (offset 3992) — now zero-pads the tail like EVM `calldataload`. With these fixes `Spec.Signature.verify` is byte-faithful to the deployed Yul on the corpus; `verifyRefined_eq_spec` stays `rfl` (deserialise and verifyRefined share the fixed primitives), so the structural bridge now rests on an executably-faithful spec. The A3.1 axiom `∀ inputs, bytecode = verifyYulModel` is therefore NO LONGER contradicted by any tested vector (the 2026-06-11 counterexample is closed). RESIDUAL: the ∀-quantified equality over ALL 4008-byte signatures is still carried by the 10-vector KAT + ~250-mutant wrong-accept screen + the executable Lean differential, NOT by a symbolic ∀ proof — which is intractable under uninterpreted SHA-256 (= A1); closing that needs an interpreted-hash engine (Kontrol/KEVM) or verified compilation (Verity). Reproduce: `make -C contracts/verification verify-bytecode` + `cd contracts/verification/lean && lake exe verify-test-vectors`.

bytecode_symbolic_rules_2026_06_10.A3.2_wallet_validate: POINTWISE-EQUIVALENCE to the Lean model (HalmosValidateUserOpEquiv, 4 rules) + per-property rules (HalmosValidateUserOp 8) on codehash 0x43c654…a06a; axiom carries the kernel-proven reachable-state hypothesis. ownerIndex coverage: rule 1 enumerates the entire installed set {0,1,2} (finite — exhaustive) + concrete reps {3,2^200,max} for the unset partition (uniform reject); rule 1c (check_validateUserOp_pointwise_installed_indices) ADDS a SYMBOLIC sweep over the installed slots {1,2}. The unset partition is NOT symbolically swept — a symbolic non-installed key NotConcreteErrors on the dynamic-bytes ownerAtIndex getter (a hard Halmos ceiling; the attempted unset-sweep rule was REMOVED because it errors). Net: the six-concrete-reps ceiling is reduced (installed slots symbolic), not eliminated.

bytecode_symbolic_rules_2026_06_10.A3.1_verifier_gates: 3 Halmos input-gate rules (boundary-swept length revert + N-mask reject) on codehash 0xf1ef…fef5. FULL FUNCTIONAL layer DISCHARGED on the corpus (2026-06-13): the EXECUTABLE Lean<->FIPS<->bytecode KAT runs full-verify 10/10 (lake exe verify-test-vectors, requireFullVerify=true, HARD CHECK — Spec.Signature.verify ACCEPTS the 4 valid vectors and REJECTS the 6 negatives, matching the deployed verifier) + bulk 384/384 (verify-bulk, 192 valid + 192 mutated vs the Rust oracle) + ~250-mutant wrong-accept screen (SPHINCsC10AsmAdversarial). The two Lean-spec reconstruction bugs (chainHash ADRS chain_pos field; loadWord32 tail zero-padding at sig offset 3992) are FIXED, so the Lean spec is now executably faithful and verifyRefined_eq_spec stays rfl over the faithful spec; FORS-htIdx binding is executably confirmed. RESIDUAL (coverage ceiling, NOT a falsity): the ∀-signature symbolic equivalence over ALL 4008-byte signatures is intractable under uninterpreted SHA-256 (=A1); see docs/A3_1_VERIFIER_GAP.md (functional layer RESOLVED).

headline_one_line: The three security claims are kernel-proven over the Lean models, and the wallet's CONTROL-FLOW surfaces are discharged on the deployed bytecode by Halmos over both compiler profiles — but the VERIFIER's full functional equivalence is NOT (the single named residual). A3.2 wallet VALIDATE: pointwise equivalence to the clause-for-clause Lean-model transcription (symbolic envelope, generic uninterpreted verifier, reachable-state invariant); the wrapper ownerIndex is covered by enumerating the entire installed set {0,1,2} + concrete reps for the unset partition + a SYMBOLIC sweep over the installed slots {1,2} (the unset partition cannot be swept symbolically — a hard Halmos dynamic-bytes-getter ceiling) + per-property rules. A3.2-exec wallet EXECUTE: pointwise equivalence of executeWithOffchainCount/executeBatchWithOffchainCount to the Lean Execute model over a SYMBOLIC (∀) ownerIndex + atomicity + credit rules. A3.3 factory: createAccount⟺precondition iff + reject rules. A3.4 owner table: add/remove/initialize pointwise vs the Lean Storage model + ownerAtIndex read parity. A3.1 verifier: discharged-bytecode on the corpus — input gates on bytecode + a FULL-functional EXECUTABLE Lean<->FIPS<->bytecode KAT (verify-test-vectors full-verify 10/10, requireFullVerify=true: accepts the 4 valid + rejects the 6 negatives) + bulk 384/384 + ~250-mutant screen; the Lean spec is now executably faithful (the chainHash/loadWord32 reconstruction bugs are fixed), with the ∀-signature symbolic equivalence the standing coverage ceiling (intractable under uninterpreted SHA-256 = A1), NOT a falsity — see docs/A3_1_VERIFIER_GAP.md. So 'fully proven to bytecode' holds for the wallet/factory/owner-table CONTROL FLOW (modulo the TCB below); the verifier's functional equivalence is carried on the corpus by the executable Lean<->bytecode KAT + bulk differential + mutant screen, not yet a ∀-symbolic proof. A1 (SHA-256) uninterpreted in every Halmos run; the uninterpreted-verifier abstraction is exactly how the wallet rules stay tractable. A2 (EntryPoint), A4 (EVM — incl. emitted-CALL byte-delivery), A5 (EUF-CMA) remain cited-TCB. Honest ceiling: a Halmos rule is a cited Halmos+z3 solver session (harness/transcription correspondences in the TCB), not a Lean proof term.
